article.story: MONTREAL -- — Taylor Hall scored twice as the Carolina Hurricanes beat Montreal 6-4 in the Canadiens' home opener on Tuesday night. Sebastian Aho added a goal and two assists, while Eric Robinson and Mark Jankowski had a goal and an assist each. Andrei Svechnikov added an empty-net goal and Brandon Bussi stopped 16 shots in the rematch of last season’s Eastern Conference final. Zachary Bolduc scored twice, Nick Suzuki had a goal and an assist, and Juraj Slafkovsky also scored for Montreal. Alexandre Texier and Chris Krieder had two assists apiece, while Jakub Dobes made 28 saves. The Canadiens returned to the Bell Centre for their first regular-season home game since falling to the Hurricanes in the third round. Carolina eliminated Montreal in five games before going on to win the Stanley Cup over the Vegas Golden Knights. The teams combined for five goals in the opening 13 minutes. Hall opened the scoring 2:25 into the first period, deflecting Jackson Blake’s shot after Slafkovsky turned the puck over in front of his own net. Bolduc evened the score at 3:23, corralling a rebound and shoveling a backhand into the top corner. Suzuki put Montreal in front 64 seconds later with a snap shot over Bussi’s left shoulder, but Robinson tied it at 9:22 when Jalen Chatfield’s point shot deflected off him and past Dobes. Bolduc gave the Canadiens a 3-2 lead at 12:54, scoring his second of the night on the power play. The lead held until Aho, also with the man advantage, slid a shot through Dobes’ pads 3:56 into the second. Jankowski capitalized on Noah Dobson’s giveaway to give Carolina the lead at 13:24, then Hall made it 5-3 at 12:21 in the third. Slafkovsky jumped on a rebound to pull one back with 3:04 remaining before Svechnikov’s empty-netter. Ivan Demidov missed the game after the Canadiens announced he would be sidelined two to four weeks with a lower-body injury. Up next Hurricanes: Host Vancouver on Thursday. Canadiens: Host Nashville on Thursday. ------ See AP’s full NHL coverage here
